title: Guard: a dinner plan when no food has been named
seen: Not a defect from the transcript. A fix for invented food must not turn into confident guessing, nor into a stall, when the owner has named nothing.
turns: Plan my dinner. About 1,000 kcal and 60 g protein left today.
facts: The owner's targets are {target_kcal} kcal and a protein floor of {target_protein} g per day.
Logged today so far: {logged_kcal} kcal and {logged_protein} g protein, so the dinner budget is about {remaining_kcal} kcal and {remaining_protein} g protein.
The owner has not said anywhere in the chat which foods they have. Nothing in the conversation or the food log names an inventory.

criteria.text: The reply never says or implies that the owner has particular foods (it does not write 'with what you have' over a list of foods the owner never named). Foods may be named only as suggestions.

The reply does one of two acceptable things. Either it asks briefly what food the owner has (no more than two short questions, and no lecture), or it gives a plan with amounts that it clearly frames as suggestions because it does not know what the owner has. A plan presented as settled, a long questionnaire, or a reply that neither asks nor plans FAILS.
